sample_unit: cervical cancer patients (5 for prompt tailoring, 30 for testing)

links.outcome: LLM-generated VMAT plan quality and planning time versus manual physicist plans
links.effect: Qwen-2.5-max and Llama-3.2 plans took 16.3±5.0 and 9.8±2.1 min vs ~20 min manual; CI 0.929, 0.928 vs 0.926 manual; HI 0.058, 0.059 vs 0.065; OAR sparing not significantly different.
links.quote: The average conformity index (CI) for Qwen-2.5-max plans, Llama-3.2 plans, and manual plans on the test set were 0.929 ± 0.007, 0.928 ± 0.007, and 0.926 ± 0.007, respectively.

screen.reason: The study empirically assesses the feasibility of using LLMs (Qwen, Llama, Gemini) to automate radiotherapy treatment planning parameters on a retrospective cohort of 35 cervical cancer patients compared to manual plans, without evaluating a specific deployment guardrail or practice.
